# Sending into an instance's message bus, and reading it back

Every send carries a mandatory dedup key. Replaying that key returns the
original message rather than creating a second one, and the instance's history
shows what was actually accepted.

## The template

```yaml
name: message-bus-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: ops/note
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        text: {type: string}
      required: [text]
nodes:
  - type: reader
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/note
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            source: "{{messages.ops/note.text}}"
```

## The dedup key is mandatory

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"ops/note","payload":{"text":"one"}}'
# 400 — the error names Idempotency-Key
```

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: audit-1" \
  -d '{"type":"ops/note","payload":{"text":"one"}}'
# 201, returning the message's own id
```

## Replaying a key

```bash
# same key, identical body
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: audit-1" \
  -d '{"type":"ops/note","payload":{"text":"one"}}'

# same key, different body
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: audit-1" \
  -d '{"type":"ops/note","payload":{"text":"different body, same key"}}'
```

Both return the id the first send created. A replay neither duplicates the
message nor smuggles a second body in under an already-accepted key.

Downstream nodes consume only the bodies the bus actually accepted.

## Read the history

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages"
```

The history lists each distinct send, attributed to the operator who sent it.
Three sends under one dedup key leave one row, not three: the history reflects
the identities the bus actually minted.

Read it through this route. `rimsky messages tail` without `--follow` prints
only the newest row and drops the older ones — it de-duplicates against a
watermark that assumes ascending arrival while the route answers newest-first.

## Fetch one message by id

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/messages/$MESSAGE_ID"
```

Returns the row with its body and the instance it belongs to. An id that was
never minted answers 404, so an operator can tell "no such message" from "a
message with nothing in it".

`rimsky messages show <id>` retrieves the same message by id correctly.
